SMTO-PRX-0014 — SMTO couldn't confirm your Proxmox server's security certificate

GUID: e581f15e-3172-4425-84a6-daa164809a80
Slug: proxmox-tls-error
Domain: PRX · Subsystem: prx

What happened

  • SMTO tried to open a secure connection to your Proxmox server but couldn't confirm the server is who it claims to be. It stopped instead of using that connection.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store, select your Proxmox parameter, and check that "server" is the exact name the Proxmox certificate was issued for, not a different nickname or address. A certificate only matches the exact name it was made for.
  2. Ask the person who manages Proxmox to install a trusted certificate on it, or to add Proxmox's own certificate authority to the trusted list on the computer running the Gateway. Proxmox's built-in certificate isn't trusted by other computers until someone sets that up.
  3. Check that the date and time on the computer running the Gateway are correct. A wrong clock can make a valid certificate look expired or not yet valid.

What success looks like

  • The Agent connects and shows your VM list or status without a certificate error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages Proxmox or SMTO. Don't turn off certificate checking to get past this; it would let an impostor server receive your Proxmox password.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway's HTTPS connection to the Proxmox base URL failed with a TLS error (certificate trust, hostname mismatch or handshake failure).

What this means

  • The HTTP transport result carries a TLS-related error_kind and the Proxmox adapter classifies it as a TLS failure. Proxmox task and resource receipts own effect truth. A failed read, expired local wait or invalid response does not undo a mutation; diagnostics never replay writes or escalate graceful shutdown to forced stop.

Why this can happen

  • The HTTP transport result carries a TLS-related error_kind and the Proxmox adapter classifies it as a TLS failure.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the underlying TLS kind to distinguish trust, handshake and route errors before replacing certificates.

How to fix it

  • Inspect transport_error_kind in Technical details. Make sure the profile's server value matches a name in the certificate, and that the Gateway host trusts the issuing CA (install a trusted certificate on PVE, or add the PVE cluster CA to the Gateway host's system trust store). Keep verify_tls true; do not disable verification to bypass the failure.
  • Resolve the recorded TLS trust or handshake failure for the exact endpoint; retain certificate verification.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended endpoint completes verified TLS under the configured trust policy.

What not to do

  • Do not automatically disable certificate verification or trust an unverified replacement identity.

Technical notes

  • Proxmox task and resource receipts own effect truth. A failed read, expired local wait or invalid response does not undo a mutation; diagnostics never replay writes or escalate graceful shutdown to forced stop.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
